description: Add a bounded, Agent-owned Slack reply guard in the Runner for turns that finish without a Runner-observed reply action attempt.

tasks.title: Add Runner-local reply-action observation and bounded guard coordinator
tasks.description: Add the shared Runner reply-guard coordinator and its per-turn observation state. Detect the existing mo slack message send invocation from the normalized Pi/OpenCode tool_call.started observation and mark it attempted before the action can return success or failure. Keep the predicate, reminder count, timeout, and error containment in Runner code; do not add a ServerConnection probe, Server endpoint, SlackOutboxStore query, delivery lookup, persistence schema, or Server test dependency.
acceptanceCriteria: A valid Slack execution context and reply anchor make a turn eligible; absent or malformed context bypasses the coordinator.

The Runner-local predicate recognizes the existing mo slack message send invocation in the normalized Pi and OpenCode tool-call start shapes, and the attempt marker is set before action completion is known.

A reply action that later returns non-zero, is rejected, or is interrupted still counts as an attempt; final text, unrelated tool output, terminal facts, liveness, Server outbox state, and provider delivery do not count.
Coordinator state explicitly contains replyActionAttempted, remindersIssued, and a closed/evaluating/advisory-running phase, with a default reminder budget of exactly two.

The coordinator increments remindersIssued before each advisory, stops on an attempt, stops after two completed silent opportunities, and cannot open a third opportunity through duplicate or late signals.

The advisory prompt reuses the existing Slack context, reply anchor, collaboration skill, runtime session, and work directory; it permits deliberate silence and never creates reply content or publishes through the Server on the Agent's behalf.
Each advisory has a finite abortable bound. Timeout, failure, unavailable runtime, interruption, and late completion preserve the original result and never retry the advisory or original turn.

Runner unit tests cover Pi and OpenCode attempt observation, rejected-send attempts, final-output-only turns, default-two budgeting, explicit silence, duplicate terminal signals, timeout/failure/unavailable/interrupted paths, and non-Slack bypass.
The focused Runner typecheck and reply-guard/runtime test suites pass.
tasks.output: A tested Runner-local reply-action observation tracker and shared two-reminder reply-guard coordinator with bounded abortable advisory behavior.
tasks.notes: The authoritative fact is a local action invocation attempt, not Server acceptance. Keep the normalized event predicate aligned with the existing Pi and OpenCode observer shapes.

tasks.title: Guard initial Pi and OpenCode AgentJob terminal turns
tasks.description: Integrate the shared Runner reply guard into the initial AgentJob turn boundary after the original Pi or OpenCode runtime result and observer work are terminal and drained. Pass the same turn observation tracker into the coordinator, preserve the original WorkItemResult, and keep Slack liveness finalization independent.
acceptanceCriteria: Initial AgentJob turns with a valid Slack execution context and reply anchor are evaluated for both Pi and OpenCode only after their runTurn result is terminal, while non-Slack and malformed-context turns retain existing behavior.

A terminal turn with an existing reply action invocation, including a send that later fails, receives no advisory; final assistant text, unrelated tools, runtime events, and liveness facts alone do not suppress or trigger the guard except through the reply-action start predicate.

An unpublished eligible turn receives up to the shared default-two bounded advisories that ask the Agent to publish a self-contained conclusion through the existing reply action or deliberately remain silent, reuse the current runtime session and supplied anchor, and do not synthesize Server-authored content.

The advisory uses the existing Pi/OpenCode follow-up path with the original work directory and shared observation tracker, combines the original cancellation signal with a finite timeout, and claims reminder state before awaiting runtime work.

Timeout, invocation failure, runtime unavailability, interruption, or an attempted reply during an advisory preserves the original success, failure, cancellation, deadline, or unknown WorkItemResult and does not rerun the original turn or retry the advisory.

Initial AgentJob tests cover Pi and OpenCode unpublished turns, accepted and rejected reply-action attempts, Agent-authored reply, explicit silence, two-reminder exhaustion, duplicate terminal evaluation, guard failures/timeouts, non-Slack bypass, and unchanged report/liveness output.
The focused Runner typecheck and AgentJob/runtime test suites pass.
tasks.output: Initial AgentJob Pi/OpenCode integration with preserved WorkItemResult and Runner-local bounded reply reminders.
tasks.notes: Use existing command-runtime helpers and runtime-specific interruption semantics. The internal advisory is not a second user-originated session input or Agent turn.

tasks.title: Guard Slack follow-ups at actual terminal completion
tasks.description: Reuse the shared coordinator from the follow-up handler, but separate follow-up admission from terminal completion. Preserve the existing immediate admission acknowledgement and operation journal behavior, then wait for the runtime-specific terminal completion before flushing observer facts, running the guard, and recording terminal session.activity.
acceptanceCriteria: Slack follow-up turns with a valid context and anchor invoke the same guard for OpenCode and both Pi branches, and the guard runs only after actual terminal completion rather than after follow-up admission.
Pi idle preflight(true) is treated as admission only; its completion handle settles after the background prompt continuation and terminal event reconciliation finish.

Pi streaming steer success is treated as admission only; its completion handle waits for the already-active Session turn to become terminal, and the shared observation tracker includes reply-action attempts made after steer.
OpenCode follow-up completion remains the terminal signal. Duplicate delivery, repeated terminal callbacks, and reconciliation cannot issue a second advisory or a second terminal activity record.

The follow-up advisory uses the current runtime session, work directory, observer, Slack context, anchor, and collaboration instructions, invokes no second user-originated session.input or AgentTurn, and leaves silence valid without creating a fallback reply.

Advisory timeout, failure, unavailable runtime, interruption, and late completion preserve the original follow-up outcome and still emit the existing terminal activity/liveness closeout exactly once with its original status and output payload.

Follow-up handler and runtime tests cover OpenCode completion, Pi idle/preflight completion, Pi streaming/steer completion, unpublished turns, successful and rejected reply-action attempts, Agent-authored reply, explicit silence, default-two exhaustion, duplicate delivery/terminal signals, publication during advisory, guard failures/timeouts, non-Slack bypass, and unchanged activity/liveness reporting.
The focused follow-up, runtime, and Runner integration test suites pass.
tasks.output: Slack follow-up orchestration wired to the shared Runner reply guard through real terminal completion for Pi and OpenCode, with preserved terminal activity and liveness behavior.
tasks.notes: Do not use Pi steer or preflight admission as the terminal signal. Keep the existing Slack delivery APIs and Server liveness semantics unchanged.
